text:
nora: Quick brain dump — we need a plan for heterogeneous fallback orchestration (multi-variant, per-tenant constraints, cost-aware). Keeping it lightweight at the edge but safe globally. Ideas?

diego: +1. Key constraints: no extra hop on hot path, deterministic sticky routing, and avoid global consensus.

iza: Can we encode a fallback DAG instead of a flat sequence? e.g. canary -> canary-q8 -> stable, but for some tenants skip q8. DAG lets us express branching.

cheng: DAG is nice but keep runtime simple: edges should evaluate small predicates (latency, recent error rate, token budget). Agent picks first satisfied node.

nora: Agreed. Control-plane publishes signed policy blobs with DAG + predicates + sampling seeds. Edge subscribes and keeps compact cache.

diego: For quality signals, use two-tier checks: cheap heuristics on every response and sampled golden probes async. Agent fuses them (heuristic pass + recent probe mean) before deciding.

iza: Telemetry: record decision_label, policy_id, probe_score_window, p95_ms_window, fallback_target, and a trace_id. Keep sampled pairs (input, canary_out, fallback_out) at low rate per tenant.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: pushed policy-publisher v0.1 to staging :rocket:

cheng: Safety invariants: 1) When in doubt, prefer control-plane decision; 2) Tenant-exempt list honored; 3) Max concurrent fallbacks per region enforced.

diego: Add rate-limiting and jitter on fallback actions to avoid synchronized thrash. Also backoff on rapid oscillation.

iza: Operational hooks: /policy/last, /decider/state, /force/fallback, /pin/tenant. All signed API calls.

nora: Cost-aware decisions: agent estimates token-cost delta and compute-cost delta for each variant. Decision score = w_latency*latency_gain - w_quality*quality_loss - w_cost*cost_increase. Policy exposes weights.

cheng: Make weights editable per-tenant for enterprise customers. Default to latency-first for PLG.

diego: Implementation sketch: small Go library (decider) with: policy cache, sticky hash map, probe harness (async), lightweight heuristics, telemetry emitter. Median decision latency target with cache <2ms.

ops-bot: infra-bot: created ticket RW-1502 for decider lib and perf targets :white_check_mark:

iza: Test matrix: mirrored traffic run (2w), golden-probe latency injection, noisy-neighbor stress test, tenant-exempt smoke. Measure: quality delta, p95, fallback churn, cost delta.

nora: Edge-state machine: NORMAL -> SOFT -> HARD -> LOCKED. Every transition emits an event and increments a rollback counter. Keep transitions idempotent.

cheng: For correctness: sign and version policies; agents verify signature and check nonce to avoid replay. Audit every policy push.

diego: On policy upgrade, send a brief warmup period where agents shadow-decide for N minutes before enforcing. Helps catch bad predicates.

iza: Debugging UX: single-pane view with recent decisions per region + sample pairs + policy blob diff. Also quick command to pin route for a tenant for 24h.

nora: Runbook short list: freeze-autofallback, force-unlock-tenant, escalate to eng-runtime, rollback policy, region-disable. Keep steps < 8 actions.

cheng: Small extension: decider exposes a write-only local queue of suspicious samples for golden scorer to prioritize. Limits ensure we don't overload scorer.

diego: Security: policy pushes must be RBACed; only a small group can flip the global kill-switch. Log and alert on any mass fallback events.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: RFC created https://github.com/redwood/research/issues/2101 with proto + experiment plan :memo:

nora: Action items: nora to draft policy proto (DAG + predicates + weights), diego to prototype Go decider, iza to design telemetry schema and debug UI, cheng to write runbook. We'll sync next week.

nora: Thanks all — aim to keep the decider minimal but expressive.
